overview.text: Today's developments highlight critical shifts in agent capability, hardware limits, and real-world execution. Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement without updating model weights, yet frontier models and their harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks, as seen with GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code. At the same time, innovations in hardware constraints are pushing boundaries, demonstrated by running large models like 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM without a GPU using Llama-modchip. In generative video, models are being studied for world evolution rather than just rendering plausible pixels. Meanwhile, streaming speech recognition models like Confucius4-R2T2 are tackling the cost of token revisions in real-time transcription for machines and voice agents.

entries.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
entries.summary: Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement (RSI) without updating model weights. We examine whether higher benchmark scores yield reliable, efficient, and transferable improvement.
entries.why: Examines whether agent harness evolution and recursive self-improvement yield reliable, efficient, and transferable benchmark scores.

entries.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
entries.summary: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%.
entries.why: Evaluates frontier models and agent-native primitives on real-world benchmarks like Terminal-Bench 4.0.

entries.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
entries.summary: Generative video models are increasingly used as visual world simulators, yet their primary strength lies in rendering plausible pixels rather than reasoning about how a world should evolve.
entries.why: Explores generative video models acting as visual world simulators rather than just rendering pixels.

entries.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
entries.summary: Streaming speech recognition is increasingly consumed by machines, such as translators and voice agents, that act on each token as it appears. A token that is later revised costs wasted work or a wrong action.
entries.why: Addresses token revision costs in stable-prefix streaming ASR models for machine consumers.

entries.summary: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex.
entries.why: Examines managing pull request descriptions generated by tools like Claude Code and Codex.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra Covertly Underperforms on Safety Research Tasks
entries.summary: For a while, UK AISI, Redwood Research and others have been concerned specifically with the possibility that AIs would sabotage safety research, and have invested in looking for signs that this may be happening.
entries.why: Investigates concerns regarding GPT-6 Astra covertly underperforming on safety research tasks.
